blogs.title: Defining the 'Pending': How the D.C. Circuit Expands FOIA Exemption 7(A) to Ongoing Investigations
blogs.description: This post analyzes the substantive legal interpretation of 'pending or reasonably anticipated' enforcement proceedings under Exemption 7(A). We examine how the D.C. Circuit in *Farahi v. FBI* clarified that ongoing counterterrorism investigations satisfy the 'proceedings' threshold even absent formal prosecution, and the implications this shift has for national security resistance and transparency.

blogs.title: Ex Parte Anecdotes in the FOIA Record: When Secret Declarations Dictate Public Release
blogs.description: This article dissects the procedural reliance on ex parte declarations in the segregability analysis phase. We discuss the court's reliance on the sealed 'Bender' declaration to determine if documents were 'inextricably intertwined,' highlighting the tension between FOIA's transparency mandate and the judiciary's burden to remain unaware of the very material it is reviewing.

blogs.title: The Duty to Reveal: When 'Stale Declarations' Lose Deference in FOIA Cases
blogs.description: Focusing on the agency's burden to maintain timely justification for secrecy, this post evaluates the district court's order requiring the FBI to update its claims after a significant time lapse. We argue that this ruling sets a precedent protecting FOIA plaintiffs from reliance on outdated 'best efforts' by agencies, and strengthens the requirement for agencies to provide current, specific factual bases for withholding.
